sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Benjamin Poulin，我是Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店打碟时期，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: Today, military footage of flying objects that can't be explained.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将讨论那些无法解释的飞行物体的军事影像。

sentences.en: A decade of hidden funding in the government budget.
sentences.zh: 政府预算中长达十年的隐秘资金。

sentences.en: A Times investigation discovers a secret program inside the Pentagon to investigate the threat of UFOs.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的一项调查发现，五角大楼内部存在一个调查不明飞行物（UFO）威胁的秘密项目。

sentences.en: It's Monday, December 18th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月18日，星期一。

sentences.en: Helene, you cover the Pentagon for The Times and my sense is that it's a very secretive organization that holds information tightly.
sentences.zh: Helene，你负责报道五角大楼，我的感觉是，那是一个非常封闭、严守信息的组织。

sentences.en: I assume a lot of your reporting is built around confidential sources, right?
sentences.zh: 我想你的很多报道都是建立在机密消息来源基础上的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, an enormous amount of my reporting is built on confidential sources, but usually the tips that I get and the stories that I am chasing tend to be about airstrikes,
sentences.zh: 是的，我绝大部分的报道都依赖于机密消息来源，但通常我得到的线索和追踪的故事往往是关于空袭，

sentences.en: about things that the military is doing around the world, about North Korea, about Niger, Syria, Iraq.
sentences.zh: 关于军方在世界各地采取的行动，关于朝鲜、尼日尔、叙利亚、伊拉克等问题。

sentences.en: But recently, I got a tip and found myself chasing a story that took me completely in a different direction than anything I had ever tried to do before.
sentences.zh: 但最近，我收到了一条线索，发现自己正在追踪一个故事，它把我带向了一个与我以往尝试过的任何事情都完全不同的方向。

sentences.en: And after a series of phone calls, I found myself in a nondescript hotel lobby near Union Station in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 经过一系列电话沟通，我最终在华盛顿特区联合车站附近的一家不起眼的酒店大堂里，

sentences.en: with a high-level intelligence source from the Pentagon.
sentences.zh: 见到了来自五角大楼的一位高级情报消息人士。

sentences.en: Oh boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I've spent a good portion of, if not all of my career, pretty much remaining in the shadows.
sentences.zh: 我职业生涯的大部分时间，甚至可以说全部时间，几乎都是在阴影中度过的。

sentences.en: For me, that was more of a professional necessity.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这更多是一种职业上的必要。

sentences.en: Luis Elizondo, who had just resigned his job at the Defense Department, he's an intel officer, so these are a totally different breed of people.
sentences.zh: Luis Elizondo，他刚刚辞去了国防部的职务，他是一名情报官员，所以这些人是完全不同的一类人。

sentences.en: They tend to be really spooky guys.
sentences.zh: 他们往往是非常神秘的家伙。

sentences.en: They're very secretive.
sentences.zh: 他们非常谨慎。

sentences.en: They tend to be more paranoid.
sentences.zh: 他们往往更加多疑。

sentences.en: There was a lot of looking over to make sure nobody was seeing us.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多环顾四周的动作，以确保没有人看到我们。

sentences.en: He sat with his back to the wall.
sentences.zh: 他背对着墙坐着。

sentences.en: He said because he wanted to see if anybody came in.
sentences.zh: 他说是因为他想看看有没有人进来。

sentences.en: There was a lot of that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多类似这样的举动。

sentences.en: But when you put all of that aside, what came out of his mouth was absolutely extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 但当你把所有这些抛开，他口中所说的一切绝对是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: He sat across the table from me in this hotel lobby and said that he had been running a program at the Pentagon looking into UFOs.
sentences.zh: 他坐在酒店大堂里我的对面，说他曾在五角大楼负责一个调查UFO的项目。

sentences.en: UFOs.
sentences.zh: UFO。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what I thought.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时也是这么想的。

sentences.en: Can you just explain the name of the program?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下这个项目的名称吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program.
sentences.zh: “先进航空航天威胁识别计划”。

sentences.en: And why threat?
sentences.zh: 为什么要叫“威胁”？

sentences.en: Well, in the Department of Defense, keep in mind, the name of the department is the Department of Defense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在国防部，请记住，这个部门的名字就叫国防部。

sentences.en: It's a national security organization.
sentences.zh: 它是一个国家安全组织。

sentences.en: Its job is to identify and, if necessary, neutralize any threats to U.S.
sentences.zh: 它的工作是识别并（如有必要）消除任何对美国国家安全的威胁。

sentences.en: national security.
sentences.zh: 国家安全。

sentences.en: It is a very significant mission of the department.
sentences.zh: 这是该部门非常重要的使命。

sentences.en: So typically missions in the department involve fighting wars and identifying threats, whether they be chemical threats, biological threats, missile threats, you name it.
sentences.zh: 所以该部门的任务通常涉及战争和识别威胁，无论是化学威胁、生物威胁、导弹威胁，应有尽有。

sentences.en: Any threat du jour, right?
sentences.zh: 任何当下的威胁，对吧？

sentences.en: In this particular case, advanced aerospace threats.
sentences.zh: 在这个特定案例中，就是先进的航空航天威胁。

sentences.en: This is a program to try to identify UFOs.
sentences.zh: 这是一个试图识别UFO的项目。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a program to investigate sightings of UFOs, particularly among military service members, pilots, Navy pilots, Air Force pilots, and to chronicle them.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个调查UFO目击事件的项目，特别是针对军方人员、飞行员、海军飞行员、空军飞行员，并对这些事件进行记录。

sentences.en: And also to look at the technology involved in some of the objects in the hopes of eventually being able to reverse engineer the things that these people believe that they have seen.
sentences.zh: 同时也是为了研究其中涉及的技术，希望能最终对这些人认为自己所见到的东西进行逆向工程。

sentences.en: These are very, I believe, very compelling videos.
sentences.zh: 我相信这些视频非常有说服力。

sentences.en: What you're looking at is what the pilots and the control operators are looking at when they're looking at the computer screen during the middle of an F-18 flight.
sentences.zh: 你现在看到的是飞行员和控制操作员在F-18飞行过程中查看电脑屏幕时所看到的内容。

sentences.en: There's a whole fleet of them.
sentences.zh: 那里有一整队这样的物体。

sentences.en: Look on the ASA.
sentences.zh: 看ASA（空对空雷达）。

sentences.en: They're all going against the wind.
sentences.zh: 它们都在逆风飞行。

sentences.en: The wind's 120 knots from the weSt.
sentences.zh: 风速是来自西方的120节。

sentences.en: Don't look at that thing, dude.
sentences.zh: 别看那个东西，伙计。

sentences.en: They're seeing an object that seems to have a force field, as they describe it, around it,
sentences.zh: 他们看到一个物体，正如他们所描述的那样，周围似乎有一个力场，

sentences.en: that's hovering before it suddenly disappears out of the sky as soon as they think that they're getting a radar lock on it.
sentences.zh: 它在盘旋，一旦他们认为雷达锁定了它，它就会立刻从天空中消失。

sentences.en: That's not an LNS, though, is it?
sentences.zh: 那不是LNS（低噪声源），对吧？

sentences.en: It's not an LNS, dude.
sentences.zh: 那不是LNS，伙计。

sentences.en: Well, if there's a little thing, it's rotating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果有个小东西，它在旋转。

sentences.en: So, Helene, it sounds like the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program is interviewing American military personnel, including pilots,
sentences.zh: 那么，Helene，听起来“先进航空航天威胁识别计划”是在采访包括飞行员在内的美国军事人员，

sentences.en: who have seen things that they can't quite identify and that that's part of the evidence gathering.
sentences.zh: 那些见过他们无法识别的东西的人，而这也是证据收集的一部分。

sentences.en: That is part of the evidence gathering.
sentences.zh: 这确实是证据收集的一部分。

sentences.en: So what this particular video demonstrates is an object otherwise referred to as a tic-tac by some of the pilots.
sentences.zh: 所以这个特定的视频展示的是一个被一些飞行员称为“Tic-Tac”（嘀嗒糖）的物体。

sentences.en: It's a small white craft to the untrained observer.
sentences.zh: 对于未经训练的观察者来说，它是一个白色的小飞行器。

sentences.en: It might not look like anything but a blurry little dot.
sentences.zh: 它看起来可能只是一个模糊的小点。

sentences.en: Is that why it's called a tic-tac?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它被称为“Tic-Tac”吗？

sentences.en: It literally looks like a tic-tac?
sentences.zh: 它看起来真的像一颗嘀嗒糖吗？

sentences.en: It literally looks like a tic-tac, yes.
sentences.zh: 它看起来确实像一颗嘀嗒糖，是的。

sentences.en: It literally is an object that has no flight surfaces, no apparent type of thrust mechanism, something that is hovering, something that is demonstrating extreme maneuverability,
sentences.zh: 它确实是一个没有飞行表面、没有明显推进机制的物体，它在盘旋，表现出极端的机动性，

sentences.en: sudden accelerations beyond the g-forces of what we would consider, you know, healthy acceleration, and velocities that are very, very compelling to us.
sentences.zh: 突然加速超过了我们认为健康的重力加速度，其速度对我们来说非常有说服力。

sentences.en: So in other words, it's moving in a way that does not resemble anything human-made.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它的移动方式不像任何人类制造的东西。

sentences.en: Right, something that would be, for example,
sentences.zh: 没错，比如，

sentences.en: sitting in a complete hover and then all of a sudden darts off screen at an incredible velocity that if you don't know what you're looking at,
sentences.zh: 它悬停在空中，然后突然以惊人的速度冲出屏幕，如果你不知道自己在看什么，

sentences.en: it may look like the screen just kind of pans away.
sentences.zh: 看起来可能就像屏幕平移了一样。

sentences.en: But in reality, that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 但实际上并非如此。

sentences.en: What you're looking at is an object that's moving off of the field of view at a very far distance away at an incredible velocity.
sentences.zh: 你看到的是一个物体在极远的距离外以惊人的速度移出了视野。

sentences.en: And what do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有何看法？

sentences.en: Well, speaking to you, not as someone from the Department of Defense, I think it's very curious.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不是以国防部人员的身份对你说话，我认为这非常令人好奇。

sentences.en: I would submit to you, I haven't seen anything that can do that.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，我还没见过能做到这一点的事物。

sentences.en: And I think many people who've witnessed this would agree.
sentences.zh: 我想许多目击过的人也会同意这一点。

sentences.en: So these videos are just what's been declassified.
sentences.zh: 所以这些视频只是已经解密的部分。

sentences.en: I understand you can't talk about what is classified, but is this just a small percentage of what this program has documented and collected and seen?
sentences.zh: 我明白你不能谈论机密内容，但这只是该项目记录、收集和观察到的一小部分吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Killing, did you believe him when he said this?
sentences.zh: Killing，当他说这些话时，你相信他吗？

sentences.en: Did this seem credible at first?
sentences.zh: 起初这看起来可信吗？

sentences.en: He's completely credible.
sentences.zh: 他完全可信。

sentences.en: Yes, I did believe him.
sentences.zh: 是的，我相信他。

sentences.en: The first conversation I had with him at that hotel, we were there for about four hours, I think.
sentences.zh: 我和他在那家酒店的第一次谈话，我想我们待了大约四个小时。

sentences.en: And he's sitting and we're going through and he's showing me documents and pictures and videos and all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他坐在那里，我们逐一查看，他向我展示了文件、图片、视频以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: It seemed completely credible to me in the moment.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，这对我来说完全可信。

sentences.en: But then I get on the Metro afterwards and I'm thinking, what have I just listened?
sentences.zh: 但后来我坐地铁离开时，我在想，我刚才听到了什么？

sentences.en: And the further away I got from the interview, the less believable it seemed.
sentences.zh: 离采访越远，它看起来就越不可信。

sentences.en: You know, it's as if you're in this interview and you're hearing this stuff and it makes complete sense to you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就好像你在采访中听到这些东西时，觉得完全说得通。

sentences.en: And then you walk away and you're back in the real world.
sentences.zh: 然后你走开，回到现实世界。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'm sitting on the Metro in Washington thinking, is this actually for real?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我坐在华盛顿的地铁上想，这是真的吗？

sentences.en: So the doubts begin to creep in.
sentences.zh: 所以怀疑开始悄悄滋生。

sentences.en: The doubts begin to creep in right away.
sentences.zh: 怀疑立刻就开始滋生了。

sentences.en: But I realized pretty early on, it's not for me to determine whether UFOs exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但我很早就意识到，确定UFO是否存在不是我的工作。

sentences.en: I'm a Defense Department reporter.
sentences.zh: 我是国防部的记者。

sentences.en: This is what I write about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所写的内容。

sentences.en: Once I got my head around that, it sort of made it easier for me to figure out what my reporting objective was.
sentences.zh: 一旦我想通了这一点，就更容易确定我的报道目标了。

sentences.en: And that was basically to confirm that there was a program going on at the Pentagon and to find out as much about it as I could.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是确认五角大楼确实存在这样一个项目，并尽可能多地了解它。

sentences.en: So where did this program actually come from?
sentences.zh: 那么这个项目到底是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: This crazy sounding but real secret government program?
sentences.zh: 这个听起来疯狂但确实存在的政府秘密项目？

sentences.en: It turns out that it started in 2007 through the former Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, Democrat of Nevada, who only in January ended a 30-year Senate career.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，它始于2007年，由前参议院多数党领袖、内华达州民主党人Harry Reid发起，他刚刚在1月结束了30年的参议院生涯。

sentences.en: Harry Reid has had a longtime interest in UFOs that he got from his friend Robert Bigelow.
sentences.zh: Harry Reid长期以来对UFO很感兴趣，这种兴趣源于他的朋友Robert Bigelow。

sentences.en: So Robert Bigelow is a billionaire aerospace company executive who has had an interest in UFOs for decades.
sentences.zh: Robert Bigelow是一位亿万富翁航空航天公司高管，几十年来一直对UFO感兴趣。

sentences.en: Do you believe in aliens?
sentences.zh: 你相信外星人吗？

sentences.en: I'm absolutely convinced that's all there is to it.
sentences.zh: 我绝对相信，事实就是如此。

sentences.en: He's definitely a true believer.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是一个坚定的信徒。

sentences.en: And he has said on, you know, on TV and he said to us that he believes that, you know, we're not alone.
sentences.zh: 他在电视上说过，也对我们说过，他相信我们并不孤单。

sentences.en: He believes that aliens exist and that UFOs have visited this planet.
sentences.zh: 他相信外星人存在，并且UFO已经造访过这个星球。

sentences.en: There has been and is an existing presence, an ET presence.
sentences.zh: 一直以来都存在，并且现在也存在一种外星人的存在。

sentences.en: And I spent millions and millions.
sentences.zh: 我花了几百万又几百万。

sentences.en: I probably spent more as an individual than anybody else in the United States has ever spent on this subject.
sentences.zh: 作为个人，我在这方面花的钱可能比美国任何人都多。

sentences.en: Is it risky for you to say, you know, in public that you believe in UFOs and aliens?
sentences.zh: 在公开场合说你相信UFO和外星人，这对你来说有风险吗？

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: And that's sort of where it all started.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: Within a year or so, Mr. Reid got the Defense Appropriations Subcommittee to put money into, black money into the Pentagon budget to fund a program to look into this.
sentences.zh: 大约一年内，Reid先生让国防拨款小组委员会投入资金，即五角大楼预算中的“黑钱”，来资助一个研究这个问题的项目。

sentences.en: I mean, when you say black money, what exactly does that mean?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你提到“黑钱”时，这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: So there was $22 million that Harry Reid got for the program in 2007.
sentences.zh: 2007年，Harry Reid为该项目争取到了2200万美元。

sentences.en: He went through fellow Senators Ted Stevens and Danny Noywe from Alaska and Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 他通过了参议员同事Ted Stevens和Daniel Inouye（来自阿拉斯加和夏威夷）。

sentences.en: And they were able to slip this into the Defense Intelligence Agency funding.
sentences.zh: 他们成功地将这笔钱塞进了国防情报局（DIA）的资金中。

sentences.en: And that the funding for the DIA is classified anyway.
sentences.zh: 而DIA的资金本身就是机密的。

sentences.en: So that brings us back to black money.
sentences.zh: 所以这就回到了“黑钱”的问题上。

sentences.en: Black money, as it turns out, is money that Congress allocates for programs that are either classified or they don't want anybody to know about.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，“黑钱”是国会为那些要么是机密，要么不想让任何人知道的项目所分配的资金。

sentences.en: Now, we all know that there's a lot of things that the government does that they don't want the average American to know about.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们都知道政府做了很多不想让普通美国人知道的事情。

sentences.en: And that's where this comes into.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的来源。

sentences.en: It's the sort of money that you can't find in a budget line.
sentences.zh: 这是一种你在预算项目中找不到的钱。

sentences.en: When we first went looking for the program, I stupidly thought I could just call up the budget from 2007 and look at the defense appropriations.
sentences.zh: 当我们第一次去寻找这个项目时，我愚蠢地以为我可以调出2007年的预算，看看国防拨款。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to tell you how many hours I wasted trying to find it until we finally threw up our hands and gave up.
sentences.zh: 我不会告诉你我浪费了多少小时试图找到它，直到我们最终摊开双手放弃了。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until I flew to Las Vegas and met with Harry Reid and he told me on the record about getting this funding for the program that I really actually believed that it existed.
sentences.zh: 直到我飞往拉斯维加斯与Harry Reid会面，他正式告诉我关于为该项目获得这笔资金的事，我才真正相信它的存在。

sentences.en: So this is a very secret and not highly regarded program within the defense world.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个在国防领域非常秘密且不受重视的项目。

sentences.en: So why were these three senators on board, as best you can tell?
sentences.zh: 那么据你所知，为什么这三位参议员会加入呢？

sentences.en: Well, Harry Reid said to me during our interview that when he went to Ted Stevens to talk to him about the program,
sentences.zh: 嗯，Harry Reid在采访中告诉我，当他去找Ted Stevens谈论这个项目时，

sentences.en: he said it was like pushing on an open door that Senator Ted Stevens was immediately interested in and told him that when he was a U.S.
sentences.zh: 他说这就像推开一扇虚掩的门，参议员Ted Stevens立刻产生了兴趣，并告诉他，当他还是二战时期的美国陆军飞行员时，

sentences.en: Army pilot back in World War II, he had had an experience where he thought that he was trailed by an object for miles in the air that he never knew what was.
sentences.zh: 他曾有过一次经历，他认为自己被一个物体在空中跟踪了数英里，但他从未知道那是什么。

sentences.en: And he thought immediately that this is something that the United States government should be looking into.
sentences.zh: 他立刻认为这是美国政府应该调查的事情。

sentences.en: But that was never really followed up on.
sentences.zh: 但这件事从未真正得到跟进。

sentences.en: He told his immediate superiors about it, but it never went anywhere after that.
sentences.zh: 他告诉了他的直属上司，但之后就不了了之了。

sentences.en: So like many of these pilots, he'd seen something and didn't quite understand what he'd seen.
sentences.zh: 所以像许多这样的飞行员一样，他见过一些东西，但不完全理解他所看到的东西。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why do you think that the man who used to run this program agreed to talk about it publicly with the Times?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么曾经负责这个项目的人同意与《纽约时报》公开谈论它？

sentences.en: I think he was frustrated.
sentences.zh: 我想他很沮丧。

sentences.en: The program is secret and the people who are operating it tend to be true believers.
sentences.zh: 这个项目是秘密的，而负责运营它的人往往是真正的信徒。

sentences.en: And they've complained about excessive secrecy, they say.
sentences.zh: 他们抱怨过度的保密，他们说。

sentences.en: And they also complain that in the greater world of the Pentagon, they are laughed at and sometimes ridiculed by people who have,
sentences.zh: 他们还抱怨说，在五角大楼的更大范围内，他们被那些人嘲笑，有时甚至被嘲讽，

sentences.en: who don't believe that we should be looking into that sort of research.
sentences.zh: 那些不相信我们应该进行这类研究的人。

sentences.en: Or military chain of command who they say are afraid of investigating or launching investigations into some of these sightings
sentences.zh: 还有军队指挥链中的人，据说他们害怕调查或发起对其中一些目击事件的调查，

sentences.en: because they think that that's going to interfere with their promotions once they start becoming known as, you know, a commanding general who's interested in UFOs.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为一旦自己被贴上“对UFO感兴趣的指挥官”的标签，就会影响到他们的晋升。

sentences.en: So two months ago, Elizondo got fed up and he wrote a letter of resignation to Defense Secretary Jim Mattis,
sentences.zh: 所以两个月前，埃利桑多忍无可忍，向国防部长吉姆·马蒂斯递交了辞职信，

sentences.en: complaining about the lack of support for the program and saying that excessive secrecy was preventing people from being able to do their jobs.
sentences.zh: 抱怨该项目缺乏支持，并称过度的保密使得人们无法正常开展工作。

sentences.en: Look, the folks over at DOD are absolutely some of the finest individuals I have ever had the pleasure and honor to serve with.
sentences.zh: 听着，国防部的人绝对是我有幸共事过的最优秀的人之一。

sentences.en: As for our secretary, Secretary Mattis, I can tell you from personal experience, he is absolutely one of the greatest leaders this nation has ever had.
sentences.zh: 至于我们的部长，马蒂斯部长，我可以凭个人经验告诉你，他绝对是这个国家有史以来最伟大的领导人之一。

sentences.en: The secretary inherited a department that historically was never really organized or set up to deal with a challenge like this.
sentences.zh: 部长接手的是一个历史上从未真正组织或建立起来去应对此类挑战的部门。

sentences.en: Keeping in mind that the secretary on a daily basis is dealing with issues from nuclear weapons, potentially in North Korea, to ISIS in Syria, to terrorism in Africa,
sentences.zh: 请记住，部长每天都要处理各种问题，从朝鲜潜在的核武器威胁，到叙利亚的ISIS，再到非洲的恐怖主义，

sentences.en: and of course, military commissions in Guantanamo Bay.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有关塔那摩湾的军事委员会事务。

sentences.en: So in defense of the department, please keep in mind that the phenomena that I was involved with is really hard to identify.
sentences.zh: 所以，为国防部辩护一下，请记住，我所参与研究的这些现象确实很难识别。

sentences.en: And not only is it hard to identify, it's even harder to define and almost impossible to discuss.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅难以识别，更难以定义，几乎无法讨论。

sentences.en: So not only were we trying to figure out exactly what the phenomena is,
sentences.zh: 所以我们不仅在试图弄清楚这些现象到底是什么，

sentences.en: but at the same time, trying to fight the forces within the department that in some cases stigmatized and delegitimized the topic.
sentences.zh: 同时也在试图对抗部门内部那些在某些情况下将这一话题污名化和非法化的势力。

sentences.en: Luke, put simply, what is the stigma?
sentences.zh: 卢克，简单来说，这种污名化是什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's a great question, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I think we're entering an era of actual evidence.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们正在进入一个实证时代。

sentences.en: We've reached a moment of critical mass of credible witnesses, and these are witnesses that are in charge of multimillion-dollar weapon platforms with,
sentences.zh: 我们已经达到了可信证人的临界点，这些证人负责操作价值数百万美元的武器平台，

sentences.en: in some cases, the highest level of security clearances under trained observers.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，他们是受过训练的观察员，拥有最高级别的安全许可。

sentences.en: And so when these individuals are trying to report something, hey, I saw this when I was flying, that can be turned around and people say,
sentences.zh: 所以当这些人试图报告某些事情时，比如“嘿，我飞行时看到了这个”，情况可能会反转，人们会说，

sentences.en: hey, look, if you're crazy, you know, there goes your flight status, right?
sentences.zh: “嘿，听着，如果你疯了，你知道的，你的飞行资格就没了，对吧？”

sentences.en: Or all of a sudden now, Commander So-and-so in charge of this very elite fighter wing will no longer be taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 或者突然之间，那位负责精英战斗机联队的某某指挥官就不再被认真对待了。

sentences.en: In fact, people are going to start to judge whether or not, maybe, you know, our friend here might not be a little bit crazy or maybe some loose screws.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们会开始评判，也许，你知道，我们这位朋友是不是有点疯，或者脑子有点问题。

sentences.en: And that's always a threat to these people's career.
sentences.zh: 这对这些人的职业生涯来说始终是一种威胁。

sentences.en: And let's face it, these people have to pay their taxes, they have to pay their mortgages, they have families, they're putting their kids through school.
sentences.zh: 面对现实吧，这些人要纳税，要还房贷，有家庭，还要供孩子上学。

sentences.en: And frankly, they're just really good patriots, and they want to do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，他们是非常好的爱国者，他们想做正确的事。

sentences.en: And that stigma is pretty powerful.
sentences.zh: 而这种污名化的力量非常强大。

sentences.en: It stops a lot of people from reporting something that maybe they would normally report.
sentences.zh: 它阻止了许多人报告他们本可能会报告的事情。

sentences.en: But you learned in this position you had at the Pentagon that many top American military pilots had seen things that they couldn't explain,
sentences.zh: 但你在五角大楼任职期间了解到，许多美国顶级军用飞行员都见过他们无法解释的事情，

sentences.en: and in many cases they had caught them on video inside their planes, but that they might have still been nervous to talk about it, right?
sentences.zh: 而且在很多情况下，他们还在飞机上拍到了视频，但他们可能仍然不敢谈论它，对吧？

sentences.en: Sure, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So you resigned because you were leading a program that couldn't really be discussed inside the Pentagon.
sentences.zh: 所以你辞职是因为你领导的一个项目在五角大楼内部根本无法讨论。

sentences.en: It was that secretive.
sentences.zh: 它就是那么保密。

sentences.en: And that wasn't being taken as seriously as you felt it needed to be and should be.
sentences.zh: 而且它没有得到你认为应该得到的重视。

sentences.en: And you wanted Defense Secretary Jim Mattis to know about it and realize how important it might be.
sentences.zh: 你希望国防部长吉姆·马蒂斯知道这件事，并意识到它可能有多重要。

sentences.en: And you felt that could only happen from the outside.
sentences.zh: 而你觉得这只能从外部实现。

sentences.en: Yes, that is absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代做夜店DJ的时候，你每天都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 佐兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Sunday, a lawyer for President Trump accused Special Counsel Robert Mueller of illegally obtaining emails and other records from the president's transition team,
sentences.zh: 周日，特朗普总统的一名律师指控特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒非法获取了总统过渡团队的电子邮件和其他记录，

sentences.en: the latest in mounting political attacks by Trump and his allies on Mueller's Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 这是特朗普及其盟友对穆勒的俄罗斯调查发起的日益激烈的政治攻击中的最新一起。

sentences.en: In a letter to Congress, the president's lawyer said that the government agency that handed the materials over to investigators
sentences.zh: 在给国会的一封信中，总统的律师表示，将这些材料交给调查人员的政府机构

sentences.en: did not allow the transition team to review the materials, which the lawyer said should have been shielded by protections like attorney-client privilege.
sentences.zh: 并没有允许过渡团队审查这些材料，律师称这些材料本应受到律师-客户特权等保护措施的保护。

sentences.en: In a rare statement, a spokesman for the special counsel defended how the emails were obtained, saying they either had the permission of the owner
sentences.zh: 特别检察官的一位发言人在一份罕见的声明中为获取电子邮件的方式进行了辩护，称他们要么获得了所有者的许可，

sentences.en: or followed the, quote, appropriate criminal process.
sentences.zh: 要么遵循了所谓的“适当的刑事程序”。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: Joining me now is the Secretary of the Treasury, Stephen Mnuchin.
sentences.zh: 现在加入我的是财政部长史蒂芬·姆努钦。

sentences.en: And welcome back to Fox News Sunday.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《福克斯周日新闻》。

sentences.en: Great to be here with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Can you say flatly that Congress will pass this tax plan this week and send it to the president to sign before Christmas?
sentences.zh: 你能断言国会本周会通过这项税改计划，并在圣诞节前送交总统签署吗？

sentences.en: I can.
sentences.zh: 我可以。

sentences.en: It's a historic moment, and we're excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 这是一个历史性的时刻，我们很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: After a series of last-minute changes,
sentences.zh: 经过一系列最后一刻的修改，

sentences.en: Republicans in the White House and Congress say they have the votes to pass a final version of their $1.5 trillion tax bill as early as today.
sentences.zh: 白宫和国会的共和党人表示，他们最早在今天就有足够的票数通过他们1.5万亿美元税改法案的最终版本。

sentences.en: And you have no doubts that Congress will pass it this week?
sentences.zh: 你对国会本周会通过它没有疑问吗？

sentences.en: I have no doubt.
sentences.zh: 我毫无疑问。

sentences.en: This has been a terrific process with the House and Senate working together in conference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的过程，众议院和参议院在会议中通力合作。

sentences.en: And there's a terrific bill that's going to get to the president to sign.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常棒的法案，即将送交总统签署。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场痛苦、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
